# Results — Study 27 (Steamroller) on the real G10 carry tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly G10 3-month interbank short rates
(OECD MEI via DBnomics, % p.a.) and month-end USD FX (yfinance, USD per 1 unit) — the **same shared tape
as Study 36 (Greenback)**, so the two FX studies carry one fingerprint. The strategy is the dollar-neutral
carry book (long the high-rate, short the low-rate tercile, weights set on the prior month-end's rates),
monthly, 10 bp per unit traded. The rate-bucket diagnostic uses the same one-month lag as the
book. The offline core proves the machinery on a synthetic G10 with a known carry premium and risk-off
crashes; this is the measurement on the market. OECD MEI ends **2024-01**, so the as-of is pinned at
**2024-01-31** and never creeps; match the fingerprint below.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `WEAK` · Tradability `FRAGILE` · Crash risk? `Severe`

On 2001–2024 G10 the carry premium is **there, but thin**: high-rate currencies out-earn low-rate ones by
**+2.8%/yr** across (lagged) rate buckets, and the carry portfolio earns
**+0.8%/yr** net — but the Newey-West *t* is **+0.9** (gross
**+1.0**) and the Sharpe of **+0.22** has a bootstrap 95% CI of
**[-0.25, +0.72]** (17% of resamples negative).
The slope is the right way up and the literature's decades-long evidence stands behind it, but *this*
post-2000 sample alone cannot reject zero — exactly the carry decay the literature documents — so the
desk stamps `WEAK`, not `REAL`. The **steamroller is fully on the tape**: monthly skew
**-0.90**, worst month **-5.8%** (2008-10-31), max drawdown
**-15%** on a 3.6%-vol book — the GFC and COVID risk-offs,
arriving all at once. And the crash *resists* the desk's usual fix: vol-targeting **cuts** the Sharpe
(**+0.20 → +0.11**) and **deepens** the drawdown
(**-15% → -26%**), because the
crash is a sudden risk-off jump, not a vol build-up a trailing estimate can see — hence `Severe`.

## Data stamp

- **G10**: 9 currencies, 2001-08-31 → 2024-01-31, 270 months, as-of **2024-01-31**,
  fingerprint `ef7450ae792e` *(identical to Study 36's published tape — one tape, two studies)*

## The premium — present, priced, thin

- High-minus-low **lagged** rate-bucket spread **+2.8%/yr** (bucketed on the
  prior month-end's rate, the same information set as the book — sorting on the same month's rate is the
  classic look-ahead this diagnostic now avoids).
- Carry portfolio (net @10 bp): **+0.8%/yr** (HAC *t* =
  **+0.9**), Sharpe **+0.22**, bootstrap 95% CI
  **[-0.25, +0.72]**, vol 3.6%.
- **Turnover 0.55×/yr** — rates move slowly, so the book is genuinely cheap to run.
  Cost sweep (bp per unit → Sharpe): 0 | 10 | 25 | 50 | 100 bp → +0.24 | +0.22 | +0.20 | +0.16 | +0.08. The cost claim is now *exercised*
  on real rebalancing (the synthetic control's constant rates produce zero turnover by construction, so
  it could never test this).

## The steamroller — carry's fat negative tail

- Monthly skew **-0.90**; worst month **-5.8%**; worst-5 average
  **-3.3%**; max drawdown **-15%**. Worst months:
  2008-10-31 -5.8%, 2008-09-30 -3.2%, 2020-03-31 -3.2% — the 2008 and 2020 risk-offs, exactly where the believers' story puts them.
- The worst 5 months carry **17%** of all losing-month losses
  (120 negative months) — crash-concentrated, not diffuse.
- **Vol-managed vs plain** (shared 258-month window, after the 12-month vol burn-in — the
  plain Sharpe here differs from the headline for that reason): Sharpe
  **+0.20 → +0.11**, skew
  **-0.89 → -0.72**, worst month
  **-5.8% → -9.6%**, drawdown
  **-15% → -26%**. On the real tape
  the overlay is a strict loss: it levers up the calm 2003–07 carry build-up and rides into the 2008 jump.

Signal `WEAK`, Tradability `FRAGILE`, Crash risk? `Severe`.
